chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Four (qualities), whoever possesses them, his faith will be perfect, and even if he was (full of) sins from his head to his feet, that would not diminish his faith. He (peace be upon him) said: 'And they are truthfulness, and paying back the trusts, and bashfulness (modesty), and good character.'
ai.seo_question: What four qualities ensure the perfection of faith evenness of faith despite sins?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies truthfulness, fulfilling trusts, modesty, and good character as the four pillars that perfect faith, ensuring that even a multitude of sins do not diminish the believer's spiritual standing. This teaching highlights the Shia emphasis on *akhlaq* (moral conduct) as the visible manifestation of *iman*, suggesting that ethical integrity serves as a protective shield against the nullifying effects of other transgressions. The narration underscores the practical application of faith in daily interactions, aligning with the broader Shia tradition where character is often viewed as the fruit of belief.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad Al Hannat, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Four (things), the one who has these in him, his Emān would be perfect, and even if he was (immersed) in sins from his head to his feet, that would not incur him a loss’. Heasws said: ‘And it is the truthfulness, and paying back of the entrustments, and the bashfulness, and good manners’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from abu Wallad al-Hannat from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Whoever has four things, his belief is complete even if he is covered with sins from his top to his toes, and it will not harm him. They are truthfulness, safe return of the trust, bashfulness and excellent moral behavior.”
